objects.name: International Space Station
objects.what: Home to people from many countries since 2000; a laboratory where astronauts test how bodies, plants and materials behave without weight.

objects.name: Hubble Space Telescope
objects.what: The visible-light telescope above the air since 1990; it still takes some of the sharpest pictures of the universe.

objects.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
objects.what: Sees the X-rays of black holes, exploded stars and hot gas between galaxies. Its stretched orbit reaches a third of the way to the Moon.

objects.name: XMM-Newton
objects.what: ESA's X-ray telescope, on a long, stretched orbit since 1999.

objects.name: Fermi
objects.what: Watches the whole sky in gamma rays, the most energetic light there is.

objects.name: NuSTAR
objects.what: Focuses high-energy X-rays, from black holes and the remains of exploded stars.

objects.name: IXPE
objects.what: Measures how X-rays are polarised, which shows the shape of magnetic fields around black holes and neutron stars.

objects.name: XRISM
objects.what: Japanese-American X-ray telescope that measures the speed and make-up of hot gas.

objects.name: SPHEREx
objects.what: Maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colours, to learn about the first moment of the universe and the ices in star nurseries.

objects.name: Terra
objects.what: One of the longest-working Earth watchers: forests, fires, clouds and ice since 1999.

objects.name: Aqua
objects.what: Measures Earth's water: rain, sea ice, clouds and ocean temperature.

objects.name: Landsat 9
objects.what: Pictures of every piece of land every 16 days, part of a record going back to 1972.

objects.name: Sentinel-2A
objects.what: Europe's colour pictures of land and coasts, free for anyone.

objects.name: NOAA-20
objects.what: Passes over the poles and measures the air for weather forecasts.

objects.name: GOES-19
objects.what: Hangs over the Americas on the geostationary ring and films the weather every few minutes (GOES-East).

objects.name: GOES-18
objects.what: The western partner of GOES-19, watching the Pacific (GOES-West).

source: Orbits: CelesTrak (US Space Force data), propagated with SGP4. Earth to scale; spacecraft are not.
